key_insight: Topo-Spectral Percolation Descriptors (TSPD) can infer ion-transport pathways and dimensionality directly from a single static crystal structure by combining barrier-based migration networks with spectral graph analysis.
engineering_relevance: This provides a fast, calibration-free screening tool for identifying mechanistic bottlenecks in solid electrolytes, electrodes, membranes, and related ion-conducting materials before expensive dynamical simulations.
method: Build a periodic migration network from the crystal structure and assign physics-based edge barriers.
Analyze barrier-threshold percolation to find accessible diffusion pathways and bottlenecks.
Use the spectrum of the barrier-weighted graph Laplacian to characterize transport dimensionality and mechanism.
evidence_signal: The method was validated against AIMD ion densities and neutron diffraction for eight materials spanning 1D to 3D transport, and it reproduced the established mechanism in every case.
watch_item: TSPD is most informative for pathway-limited, direction-dependent transport and may be less definitive for strongly cooperative or nearly isotropic ion motion.
paper_title: Topo-Spectral Percolation Descriptors for Mechanistic Ion Transport Pathways from Static Crystal Structures
